newsitem.title: USA: American Exploration battles well fire.
newsitem.headline: American Exploration battles well fire.

text.p: American Exploration Co plans to drill a relief well to cut off the flow of natural gas feeding a fire on an offshore platform in the Gulf of Mexico, company officials said on Thursday.

The fire, which has been burning since Tuesday on the platform about 100 miles off the coast of Louisiana, could continue burning for another two weeks before it can be extinguished, the officials said.
"I would imagine we will go ahead with the spudding of the relief well sometime fairly early in the week next week," said American Exploration Senior Vice President Elliott Pew.

A cluster of wells feeding into the platform had been producing 7.2 million cubic feet per day of natural gas and 300 barrels per day of oil, or less than 10 percent of the Houston-based company's gas and oil production.
"The (financial) impact to American will be in the loss of production," said American Exploration Chairman Mark Andrews.

Andrews estimated the lost production will cost the company "several million" dollars in cash flow this year. The company is insured for damage to the platform and other equipment in the blowout, he said.
Angular flames shooting from the platform were diminished somewhat overnight as water from the subsea geological formation shot up briefly through the well, Pew said.

The fire was ignited as crews removed a blowout preventer from a well that had been shut in. As the safety equipment was removed, gas and sands began shooting from the well, which had been cemented in, Pew said.

A no-fly zone was established over the well and shipping was diverted away from the burning platform, U.S. Coast Guard Lt. Paul Dittman said. Plans also have been made to respond to an oil spill, although little oil has been released from the wells.
"Fortunately we have not experienced any significant environmental impact," Dittman said.
